# Amazon.com Scraper

<!-- This README is generated by .github/scripts/docs.py from the scraper code, its results/ folder and .github/scrapers.json: change those and run the script instead of editing it. -->

[![tests](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/raw/ci-status/badges/amazon-scraper.svg)](https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers/blob/ci-status/status/amazon-scraper.md)

Example scraper that collects product listing data from Amazon.com, written in Python with the [Scrapfly](https://scrapfly.io/) web scraping API. Part of [scrapfly-scrapers](../README.md).

- **Guide:** [How to Scrape Amazon.com Product Data and Reviews](https://scrapfly.io/blog/posts/how-to-scrape-amazon)
- **Code:** [`amazon.py`](amazon.py) · **Example run:** [`run.py`](run.py) · **Tests:** [`test.py`](test.py)
- **Sample output:** [Product pages](results/product.json) · [Search pages](results/search.json) · [Product reviews](results/reviews.json)

## What it scrapes

- Amazon product data
- Amazon product review data
- Amazon product search

## Functions

- `scrape_search(url, max_pages=None)` → `List[ProductPreview]`: Scrape amazon search pages product previews
- `scrape_reviews(url)` → `List[Review]`: scrape product reviews of a given URL of an amazon product
- `scrape_product(url)` → `List[Product]`: scrape Amazon.com product

The functions are `async`: run them with `asyncio.run(...)` or `await` them.

### Example

The inputs are the examples of [`run.py`](run.py) (long lists cut short):

```python
import asyncio
import amazon


async def main():
    search = await amazon.scrape_search("https://www.amazon.com/s?k=kindle", max_pages=3)
    product = await amazon.scrape_product(
        "https://www.amazon.com/PlayStation-5-Console-CFI-1215A01X/dp/B0BCNKKZ91/",
    )
    reviews = await amazon.scrape_reviews(
        "https://www.amazon.com/PlayStation-5-Console-CFI-1215A01X/dp/B0BCNKKZ91/",
    )


asyncio.run(main())
```

## Output

The functions return plain dictionaries and lists. Fields:

- **`ProductPreview`**: `url`, `title`, `price`, `real_price`, `rating`, `rating_count`
- **`Review`**: `title`, `text`, `location_and_date`, `verified`, `rating`
- **`Product`**: `name`, `asin`, `style`, `description`, `stars`, `rating_count`, `features`, `images`, `info_table`

## Scrapfly settings

`BASE_CONFIG` in [`amazon.py`](amazon.py) holds the default settings of the requests, see the [Scrape API documentation](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/getting-started):

- `unblocker` = `True`: Scrapfly's [Unblocker](https://scrapfly.io/docs/scrape-api/unblocker), its anti-bot bypass
- `country` = `"US"`: country of the proxy

## Quick start

Requires Python 3.10+ and [Poetry](https://python-poetry.org/docs/#installation).

```shell
git clone https://github.com/scrapfly/scrapfly-scrapers.git
cd scrapfly-scrapers/amazon-scraper
export SCRAPFLY_KEY="YOUR SCRAPFLY KEY"   # from https://scrapfly.io/dashboard
poetry install --no-root
poetry run python run.py                  # example scrape, saves its output in ./results
poetry run pytest test.py                 # the tests of this scraper
```

Tests: `test_product_scraping`, `test_search_scraping`, `test_review_scraping`; run one with `poetry run pytest test.py -k <test>`. `run.py` and the tests scrape the live website, so they use Scrapfly credits.
